what_its_for: Omaveloxolone is used to treat Friedreich's ataxia, a rare inherited disease that affects your nervous system and causes problems with balance, coordination, and movement. This medicine helps protect nerve and muscle cells from damage caused by the disease.
how_to_take: Take omaveloxolone by mouth once a day. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Take it on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before eating or at least 2 hours after eating. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and teenagers aged 16 and older is 150 mg (three 50 mg capsules) taken once daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have liver problems or if you experience side effects. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than 12 hours away. If it is less than 12 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store omaveloxolone capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use capsules past the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating a meal within 1 hour before or 2 hours after taking your dose, as food can reduce how well the medicine works. Avoid taking certain medicines that can interfere with omaveloxolone, including some antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines, and herbal supplements like St. John's Wort — always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all medicines and supplements you take. Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice, as it may affect the level of this medicine in your blood.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness or weakness, nausea or vomiting that does not go away, signs of fluid retention such as sudden weight gain or swelling in your legs or ankles, or changes in your heart rhythm. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medicine may harm an unborn baby.
when_it_works: Omaveloxolone does not cure Friedreich's ataxia, but it can help slow the worsening of symptoms over time. You may not notice immediate changes. It may take several weeks to months before you or your doctor can tell if the medicine is helping. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not feel different right away, and do not stop without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: This medicine is approved for people aged 16 and older. It has not been studied in children under 16 years of age. If you have liver problems, your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor your liver closely with blood tests. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for some time after stopping the medicine. It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding is generally not recommended while taking omaveloxolone. Older adults should use this medicine with the same caution as younger adults, but tell your doctor about all other health conditions and medicines you take.
